rounds.text: Shiprocket Ltd is demonstrating powerful, sustained top-line expansion, evidenced by a 41% compounded sales growth over 5 years and a 24% growth over the trailing twelve months [E13, E15]. This top-line momentum is backed by operational tightening, with yearly operating margins showing an increasing trend over the last 4 years and narrowing to -3% in Mar 2026—a remarkable 23 percentage point improvement from three years prior [E21, E23]. Crucially, this margin recovery is already translating into tangible financial health through positive cash generation, delivering Rs 53 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 35 Cr in free cash flow in Mar 2026 [E26, E27]. The balance sheet has been aggressively de-risked, with borrowings dropping sharply from Rs 345 Cr a year earlier to Rs 102 Cr in Sep 2026, leaving the company almost debt-free with a pristine debt-to-equity ratio of 0.04x [E28, E30, E44]. Furthermore, the rules-based screen registers a BUY score of 65 out of 100, supported by robust screen catalysts including 52% YoY sales growth and strong profit recovery metrics [E49, E50, E52]. Conceded: [E8] low return on equity of -2.24% against sector benchmarks, [E10] a highly elevated EV/EBITDA of 696.6x, and [E17] a trailing twelve-month profit growth contraction of -2%.

Shiprocket Ltd trades at a steep price-to-book multiple of 3.87x [E1] and 3.92x against a sector benchmark of 2.13x [E6], which is flag-rated as a negative for the stock [E45]. This rich valuation is heavily disconnected from its underlying fundamental performance, marked by negative profitability returns including an ROE of -5.1% [E12], an ROCE of -2.7% [E11], and a negative 3-year median ROE of -12% [E19]. Furthermore, enterprise value multiples stretch to an extreme EV/EBITDA of 696.6x compared to a sector benchmark of 11.68x [E10], alongside a negative P/E of -175.54x [E5]. Momentum and return profiles remain weak, evidenced by a poor Sharpe ratio of -0.51 [E40], a low interest coverage ratio [E46], and a high cost of borrowing [E48]. Conceded: compounded sales growth has reached 41% over 5 years [E13] and operating margin trends have improved over recent periods [E23]. However, trailing twelve-month profit growth has turned negative at -2% [E17], underscoring that top-line expansion has failed to translate into durable shareholder returns.

Conceded: price-to-book is 3.87x [E1] and EV/EBITDA is 696.6x [E10]. However, the bear ignores the company's aggressive and successful balance-sheet de-risking, where borrowings dropped sharply from Rs 345 Cr to just Rs 102 Cr, rendering the firm almost debt free with a debt-to-equity ratio of a minuscule 0.04x [E30, E44]. Furthermore, the bear's fixation on historical negative returns overlooks massive operational turnaround proof: operating margins have expanded by 23 percentage points over the last three years to reach -3% in Mar 2026, and quarterly margins continue an upward trajectory over the last five quarters [E21, E24]. This top-line momentum is backed by robust fundamental growth, demonstrated by a 41% 5-year compounded sales growth rate [E13] and a healthy generation of Rs 53 Cr in operating cash flow alongside Rs 35 Cr in free cash flow [E26, E27]. Finally, the rules-based screen explicitly rates the stock a buy at 65 out of 100 on the back of explosive recent performance, including a 52% year-on-year sales jump and a 103% year-on-year net profit surge [E49, E50, E52].

Conceded: borrowings dropped from Rs 345 Cr to Rs 102 Cr [E30] and operating cash flow reached Rs 53 Cr [E26]. However, this de-risking occurs alongside ongoing fundamental unprofitability, evidenced by a negative P/E of -175.54x and an extreme EV/EBITDA of 696.6x against sector benchmarks of 22.72x and 11.68x respectively [E5, E10]. The bull cites margin improvement [E21, E24], but this trajectory still leaves the yearly operating margin at -3% [E21] and trailing twelve month profit growth at -2% [E17]. Furthermore, despite multi-year sales growth [E13], the company continues to destroy shareholder value through a multi-year negative return on equity averaging -13% over 5 years [E18] and -12% over 3 years [E19]. Finally, while the quantitative screen gives a low-confidence buy score of 65 [E49], it is simultaneously weighed down by low ROE flags [E54], and the stock suffers from a poor Sharpe ratio of -0.51 [E40].
